value_stream.name: Captive Insurance, Reinsurance & Enterprise Risk Financing

fields.Trigger: Risk-financing review (VS-21.2); premium spike; board mandate

Automation Opportunity: - Loss-data analytics platform; captive-economics modeling tool; TCOR dashboard
Controls: - CTL-689: TCOR actuarially baselined (VS-21.2); business case conservative/board-approved (VS-36); success metrics defined
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-26 (insurance), VS-18 (treasury), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-36 (board), W4530 (structure)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bad-data risk**: Poor loss history → flawed captive economics; mitigated by actuarial rigor & data quality
- **Over-optimism risk**: Understated retained losses → captive under-capitalized; mitigated by conservative sensitivity

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Insurance quantify the TCOR baseline (commercial premium + retained losses + risk-mgmt cost + admin) across property/cat, liability, fleet, crime, cyber, D&O, employee — per VS-26/VS-21.2

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Treasury/Actuarial model the captive business case (loss-history analysis, predicted retained-layer loss, reinsurance cost, capital required, savings vs commercial) with sensitivity
CFO/Head of Internal Audit & Risk present the business case to the board (VS-36), obtain go/no-go, and define success metrics vs the do-nothing baseline
steps.r: CFO / Head of Internal Audit & Risk

Automation Opportunity: - Retention-layer modeling; risk-appetite/structure alignment; risk-transfer validation
Controls: - CTL-689: captive structure bona-fide insurance (risk transfer); risk-scope actuarially gated; board-approved (VS-36)
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-26 (insurance), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-79 (tax), VS-36 (board), W4529 (feasibility), W4531 (domicile)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Risk-transfer-failure risk**: Structure lacks genuine risk transfer → regulatory/tax disallowance; mitigated by bona-fide insurance design (risk-shifting/distribution)
- **Scope-overreach risk**: Captive writes risks it can't price; mitigated by actuarial scope-gating

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO / Board
steps.activity: Risk/Treasury design the captive structure (pure captive vs group/sister-captive vs protected-cell), ownership (held by BuildRight Holdings), and the risk scope it writes (e.g., property/cat retained layer, liability, fleet, cyber)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Actuarial set the retention layers (self-insured retention, captive layer, commercial/reinsurance above), aligned to risk appetite (VS-21.2) and commercial-market gaps
Risk/Legal/Tax document the strategy/structure, validate risk-transfer (real insurance, not financing-sham), and obtain board approval (VS-36)

fields.Participants: Tax (VS-79), Compliance (VS-22), Captive manager, Domiciliary regulator

Automation Opportunity: - Domicile-comparison modeling; licensing-document management; regulatory-filing tracker
Controls: - CTL-689: domicile structured-evaluated; license obtained pre-underwriting; ongoing compliance integrated (VS-22/VS-79)
Cross-references: - links to VS-100.3 (legal), VS-79 (tax), VS-22 (compliance), W4530 (structure), W4534 (service providers)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Wrong-domicile risk**: Domicile mismatched to risk/cost → friction; mitigated by structured domicile evaluation
- **Licensing-failure risk**: License denied/delayed; mitigated by experienced captive-manager & sound business plan
System Touchpoints: - Legal (VS-100.3); tax (VS-79); compliance (VS-22); captive manager service (W4534)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO / VP Legal
steps.activity: Risk/Legal/Tax evaluate domicile options (onshore IC-Philippine vs offshore Labuan/Bermuda/Cayman/Singapore etc.) on capital requirements, regulation, tax, cost, reputation, and PH-group fit
Legal/Captive Manager apply for domicile licensing (business plan, capital, governance, actuarial, fit-and-proper), and establish the regulatory relationship
Compliance/Tax set up ongoing regulatory compliance (domiciliary filings, RBC/capital-adequacy, tax), integrated to VS-22/VS-79

workflows.name: Captive Formation, Capitalization & Legal Entity Setup

Automation Opportunity: - Capital-adequacy modeling; entity/governance document management; consolidation integration (VS-17)
Controls: - CTL-689 (ensure controlled execution — Captive Feasibility, Formation & Domicile/Governance (PA-153.1).)
- CTL-689: captive actuarially capitalized (≥ domiciliary min); separately accounted (VS-17); board-formed (VS-36)
Cross-references: - links to VS-18 (treasury), VS-17 (finance), VS-79 (tax), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-36 (board), W4531 (domicile), W4535 (intercompany)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-capitalization risk**: Insufficient capital → regulatory/action; mitigated by actuarial capital model & domiciliary min
- **Capital-tying-up risk**: Capital locked in captive reduces group liquidity; mitigated by capital sizing & investment liquidity (W4533)

steps.activity: Legal/Corp Secretary form the captive legal entity (incorporation, articles, bylaws, shareholder = BuildRight Holdings), register, and establish governance docs
Treasury/Finance capitalize the captive (paid-up capital, letter-of-credit/collateral per domiciliary requirement), fund from group treasury (VS-18), and book the investment
Finance/Tax establish captive accounting (separate books, statutory accounting per domicile, PFRS consolidation VS-17), and intercompany framework (W4535)

Automation Opportunity: - ALM/investment analytics; captive-governance management; underwriting/claims oversight dashboards
Controls: - CTL-689: captive board independent w/ committees; investment policy ALM-matched; separately audited (VS-21)
Cross-references: - links to VS-36 (governance), VS-18 (treasury/investment), VS-21 (audit), VS-21.2 (risk), W4532 (formation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Asset-liability-mismatch risk**: Illiquid investments can't pay claims; mitigated by ALM investment policy & liquidity buffer
- **Governance-weakness risk**: Weak captive oversight → misuse; mitigated by independent directors & separate audit
Time Estimate: - Board quarterly; investment policy annual + ongoing

steps.activity: Board/Corp Secretary establish captive governance (board w/ independent directors, underwriting/audit/investment committees, conflict-of-interest), per VS-36 standards
Treasury/Board set the captive investment policy (asset-liability matching, liquidity for claims, safety, yield, permitted assets), and manage the captive asset portfolio (links to VS-18)
Audit/Board ensure captive oversight (separate audit VS-21, actuarial review, underwriting/claims governance), reporting to the group board (VS-36)

fields.Volume: Fronting carrier + captive manager + TPA + broker + actuary + auditor

Automation Opportunity: - Provider-performance/SLA dashboards; ceding-commission analytics; vendor scorecard (VS-67)
Controls: - CTL-689 (ensure controlled execution — Captive Feasibility, Formation & Domicile/Governance (PA-153.1).); CTL-691 (ensure controlled execution — Captive Claims, Finance, Regulatory & Portfolio Analytics (PA-153.3).)
- CTL-689: fronting carrier solvent/admitted; providers contracted w/ SLA (VS-34); TPA claims-quality monitored (VS-26.3)
Cross-references: - links to VS-26 (insurance/fronting), VS-34 (procurement), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-22 (compliance), VS-67 (scorecard), W4545 (claims)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fronting-cost risk**: Fronting commission erodes savings; mitigated by competitive fronting selection
- **TPA-quality risk**: Poor claims handling (VS-26.3) → customer/claimant harm; mitigated by TPA SLA & oversight
System Touchpoints: - Insurance/fronting (VS-26); procurement (VS-34); legal (VS-100.3); compliance (VS-22); vendor scorecard (VS-67)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Insurance/Procurement select & contract the fronting carrier (admitted carrier that issues policies & cedes to captive) and service providers (captive manager, TPA claims, broker, actuary, auditor) via VS-34

steps.a: VP Legal / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: Legal/Risk negotiate fronting/ceding terms (commission, retained business, limits), service-level agreements, and risk-transfer terms, ensuring admitted-paper compliance in PH
Risk/Compliance manage provider performance/compliance (fronting carrier solvency, TPA SLA, captive-manager reporting), and renew/exit via VS-34/VS-67

workflows.name: Captive Tax, Transfer Pricing & Intercompany Framework

Automation Opportunity: - Premium-pricing/TP documentation; intercompany settlement (VS-72); tax-filing automation
Controls: - CTL-689 (ensure controlled execution — Captive Feasibility, Formation & Domicile/Governance (PA-153.1).)
- CTL-689: captive premium arm's-length & risk-transferring (deductible); TP documented; intercompany settled (VS-72)
Cross-references: - links to VS-79 (tax), VS-17 (finance), VS-72 (intercompany), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-21 (audit), W4532 (formation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Premium-deductibility risk**: Captive premium not deductible (circular/cash-basis); mitigated by arm's-length pricing & risk-transfer
- **Transfer-pricing risk**: Non-arm's-length pricing → tax adjustment; mitigated by TP documentation

steps.activity: Tax/Legal set the captive tax framework (premium tax, domicile tax, PH treatment of captive premium/capital, deductibility of premium paid to captive, BEPS/transfer-pricing)
Tax/Finance establish transfer pricing for captive premiums (arm's-length pricing per profile §2 / VS-72), documented (master file/local file where applicable), and intercompany settlement
Tax/Audit manage captive tax compliance/filings (premium tax, domicile returns, PH consolidation VS-17), defend on audit (VS-79/BIR), and report to the board

Automation Opportunity: - Policy/claims/accounting integration; go-live readiness checklist; OCM adoption tracking (VS-134)
Controls: - CTL-689 (ensure controlled execution — Captive Feasibility, Formation & Domicile/Governance (PA-153.1).)
- CTL-689: implementation PMO-governed (VS-112); systems ready pre-cutover; coverage continuity at transition (VS-26)
Cross-references: - links to VS-112 (PMO), VS-27 (IT), VS-17 (finance), VS-26 (insurance), VS-134 (OCM), W4532–W4534 (setup)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Transition-gap risk**: Coverage gap during cutover; mitigated by renewal-coordinated transition & continuity
- **Systems-not-ready risk**: Go-live before systems/processes ready; mitigated by go-live readiness gate
System Touchpoints: - PMO (VS-112); IT (VS-27); finance (VS-17); insurance transition (VS-26); OCM (VS-134)

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Treasury/PMO build the implementation plan (policy issuance via fronting, captive ceding, claims handoff, accounting, reporting), per VS-112 project governance
IT/Finance stand up captive systems (policy/claims admin, accounting, reporting integrations to VS-17/VS-27), with OCM/change enablement (VS-134) for affected teams

steps.a: Head of Internal Audit & Risk / CFO
steps.activity: Risk/Insurance execute the transition (move in-scope risks from commercial to captive at renewal VS-26), verify go-live readiness, and cut over
